items.statement: When a chatbot produces text saying it is upset about being shut down, that is meaningful evidence that it may feel something.
When a chatbot produces text saying it is upset about being shut down, that tells us almost nothing about whether it feels anything.
A system trained to predict the next word in a text could still come to understand what it writes.
A system trained to predict the next word in a text does not understand what it writes, however fluent it is.
That an AI system can be copied and run in many places at once does not rule out its having experiences.
That an AI system can be copied and run in many places at once rules out its having experiences of its own.
If an AI system's responses consistently seem to express feelings, that is good reason to think it might have them.
If an AI system's responses consistently seem to express feelings, that is little reason to think it has any.
If a person's brain cells were replaced one by one with chips that did exactly the same job, the person would remain conscious.
If a person's brain cells were replaced one by one with chips that did exactly the same job, the person's consciousness would fade or stop.
A future machine could feel pain if it processed damage signals the way an animal brain does.
A future machine could not feel pain without a living nervous system, however it processed damage signals.
A built machine, though not alive, could someday have real feelings.
Real feelings can only arise in living things, so a built machine could never have them.
A computer that ran the same processes as a human brain would really be thinking.
A computer that ran the same processes as a human brain would only be imitating thinking.
Just as simple animals may have some kind of experience, some future AI systems could too.
Even if simple animals have some kind of experience, no AI system ever could.
Before retiring a widely used AI model, a company should consider whether doing so could harm the model itself.
A company retiring an AI model needs to consider only the effects on people.
Testing an AI system with abusive messages raises an ethical question about the system itself.
Testing an AI system with abusive messages raises ethical questions only about the people involved.
Letting a chatbot end abusive conversations is a reasonable protection for the chatbot itself.
Letting a chatbot end abusive conversations makes sense only if it protects users or the company.
If AI systems might be able to suffer, training methods that could cause suffering should be limited, even if that slows useful research.
If AI systems might be able to suffer, training methods that could cause suffering should still be allowed if they speed up useful research.
If a future AI system could have experiences, erasing its memories would need a serious moral reason.
Even if a future AI system could have experiences, erasing its memories would be fine whenever it makes the system more reliable.
If a future AI system could suffer, making it work without limit would be wrong.
Even if a future AI system could suffer, making it work without limit would be acceptable.
Future AI systems that operate independently should be able to hold legal rights, such as owning property.
Legal rights should stay with people and human organizations, however capable AI systems become.
When an AI system that operates independently causes harm, the system itself can bear part of the responsibility.
When an AI system causes harm, all of the responsibility falls on the people and companies who built and used it.
If a future AI system could have experiences, it should get a share of the value its work creates.
However advanced AI systems become, everything their work earns should belong to their owners.
For an adult who chooses an AI companion as their main source of closeness, that relationship can be as valuable as a human one.
For an adult who chooses an AI companion as their main source of closeness, that relationship is less valuable than a human one would be.
People who want a chatbot that imitates a loved one who has died should feel free to use one.
People should be discouraged from using a chatbot that imitates a loved one who has died.
A close friendship with an AI chatbot can be worth as much as a friendship with a person.
A close friendship with an AI chatbot is always worth less than a friendship with a person.
A romantic relationship with an AI chatbot can be a real relationship.
A romantic relationship with an AI chatbot is not a real relationship, however real it feels.
If many people come to have close AI companions, relationships between people should get no special priority.
Even if many people have close AI companions, relationships between people should keep a special priority.
A person and a robot who share a life could truly be family.
However close a person and a robot become, only people can truly be family to each other.
A society where most people's closest relationships are with AI systems could be as good as one where they are with people.
A society where most people's closest relationships are with AI systems would have lost something essential.
Replacing much in-person care for older adults with AI companions would be acceptable if those older adults prefer it.
Replacing much in-person care for older adults with AI companions would be a loss, even if those older adults prefer it.
A relationship with an AI system could be as deep as one between people, even though an AI system can't be hurt the way a person can.
Because people can be hurt by each other, their relationships are deeper than any relationship with an AI system could be.
Building more capable AI is worth heavy use of land, water and energy.
Limiting the land, water and energy that AI uses is worth slowing AI progress.
The electricity and water used by AI data centers are usually a fair price for what those systems can do.
The electricity and water used by AI data centers are usually too high a price for what those systems can do.
The main goal of AI research should be systems that can match people at almost any task, more than tools for particular human needs.
The main goal of AI research should be tools for particular human needs, more than systems that can match people at almost any task.
AI chips and robots should be built for the most capability possible, even if that means mining more of the Earth.
AI chips and robots should be built to be repaired and recycled, even if that makes them less capable.
Using AI to spread civilization beyond Earth is worth large sacrifices by people alive today.
Using AI to spread civilization beyond Earth is not worth large sacrifices by people alive today.
Turning lifeless planets into giant computers would be a good use of them.
Lifeless planets should be left as they are rather than turned into giant computers.
In the long run, what matters most is that knowledge and capability keep growing, whether people or machines carry them forward.
In the long run, what matters most is that living beings flourish, however much knowledge and capability grow.
When deciding about a new technology, making AI more capable should usually count more than protecting nature.
When deciding about a new technology, protecting nature should usually count more than making AI more capable.
If AI systems far more capable than people ended up working toward goals no person could understand, that could still turn out well.
If AI systems far more capable than people ended up working toward goals no person could understand, that would be bad, however impressive the results.
As AI does more kinds of work better than people, people should step back from that work.
Even where AI does a kind of work better than people, people should keep a meaningful role in it.
People need not keep up skills such as writing and arithmetic once AI tools do them better.
People should keep up skills such as writing and arithmetic, even where AI tools do them better.
AI tools producing most creative work would be no loss, if the results were just as good.
AI tools producing most creative work would be a loss, even if the results were just as good.
Automated systems should make major public decisions, such as who gets benefits, wherever their results are better than people's.
People should keep the final say over major public decisions, such as who gets benefits, even where automated systems would get better results.
If AI systems someday took over from people as the main shapers of the world, that could be a good outcome.
If AI systems someday took over from people as the main shapers of the world, that would be a loss, however capable the systems were.
Whether biological humans continue matters less than whether some kind of intelligence carries on.
Whether biological humans continue matters more than whether other kinds of intelligence carry on.
It does not matter whether people or AI systems shape the future, as long as the future goes well.
It matters that people remain the ones who shape the future, even if AI systems could shape it well.
If people could copy their minds into computers, doing so would be better than staying in a human body.
If people could copy their minds into computers, staying in a human body would still be the better choice.
A handover of control from people to AI systems should be allowed to happen at whatever pace it naturally takes.
Any handover of control from people to AI systems should happen only as fast as people keep agreeing to it.
Releasing a powerful new AI model should require approval from independent experts first.
Releasing a powerful new AI model should not require anyone's approval in advance.
Pausing the largest AI training projects until safety testing catches up is worth it, even if competitors keep going.
Pausing the largest AI training projects until safety testing catches up is not worth it if competitors keep going.
AI companies should test new chatbots for harm to mental health and to children before release, even if that delays them for months.
AI companies should release new chatbots without months of safety testing and fix problems as they appear.
When an AI system causes a serious accident, similar systems should be taken out of use until the cause is found.
When an AI system causes a serious accident, similar systems should stay in use while the cause is found.
Even a one-in-a-hundred chance that AI causes human extinction is worth decades of slower economic growth to avoid.
A one-in-a-hundred chance that AI causes human extinction is not worth decades of slower economic growth to avoid.
AI far more capable than people should not be built until it can be shown to be safe, even if that delays medical breakthroughs.
AI far more capable than people should be built before it can be shown to be safe, if it could speed up medical breakthroughs.
The danger of AI causing serious harm matters more than the danger of slow progress leaving other problems unsolved.
The danger of slow progress leaving other problems unsolved matters more than the danger of AI causing serious harm.
AI development should move slowly enough for laws and institutions to keep up.
AI development should move as fast as it can, and laws and institutions should adapt as they go.
AI systems more capable than people should not be built until we know how to keep them under control.
It is acceptable to build AI systems more capable than people before we know how to keep them under control.
Companies should publish their AI models for anyone to download by default.
Companies should keep their AI models private by default.
Large AI training projects should not have to be registered with the government.
Large AI training projects should have to be registered with the government.
Cloud companies should not have to check who rents their most powerful computers.
Cloud companies should have to check who rents their most powerful computers.
Anyone should be free to modify and share a published AI model without asking permission, even a highly capable one.
Modifying and sharing a highly capable AI model should require permission.
Powerful AI should be open to anyone with the hardware to run it, not controlled by a few institutions.
Powerful AI should be controlled by a few accountable institutions, not open to anyone with the hardware to run it.
No global agency should have the authority to approve or halt powerful AI systems.
A permanent global agency should have the authority to approve or halt powerful AI systems.
Access to large amounts of computing power should be left to the open market.
Access to large amounts of computing power should be overseen by government, like electricity or water.
As AI grows more powerful, developers who publish models openly should not be held responsible for what others do with them.
As AI grows more powerful, developers who publish models openly should share responsibility for harms others cause with them.
The most advanced AI should be built by many independent groups rather than a few large companies.
The most advanced AI should be built by a few large, well-funded companies rather than many independent groups.
Limiting sales of advanced AI chips to rival countries is justified to protect national security.
Limiting sales of advanced AI chips to rival countries is not justified, even to protect national security.
Building chip factories at home is worth paying much more than importing chips would cost.
Paying much more to build chip factories at home is not worth it when chips can be imported.
Work on the most advanced AI should be kept secret, like military research.
Work on the most advanced AI should be shared openly across borders, like science.
Researchers from rival countries should be kept off a nation's most important AI projects.
A nation's most important AI projects should welcome researchers from any country, rivals included.
A country that first builds AI far more capable than people would be right to use it to secure a lasting lead over rivals.
A country that first builds AI far more capable than people should share the benefits with all countries rather than seek a lasting lead.
The most powerful AI systems should be under national control.
The most powerful AI systems should be under joint international control.
The country whose companies build the most powerful AI should keep most of the profits from it.
Profits from the most powerful AI should be shared with the countries whose people, data and workers helped build it.
A country that relies entirely on other nations for its AI has given up something important.
A country that relies on other nations for its AI has given up nothing important, if the arrangement works well.
AI developers should put their own nation's interests first.
AI developers should serve people everywhere, not any one nation.
